articles.author: varun chaaras
articles.description:
While building a small turn-based multiplayer golf prototype, I hit a bug that completely soft-locked the game.
The ball would roll, slow down… and never actually stop.
Visually, it looked stationary.

Numerically, it was still moving.
In a turn-based multiplayer game, that’s fatal - the turn can’t advance unless the ball fully stops.
I was applying friction every update, assuming velocity would eventually reach zero.
It didn’t.
Floating-point math meant the velocity just kept approaching zero forever. The game thought the ball was still moving, so the turn never ended.
I moved all physics logic into the authoritative game logic and added a hard “snap-to-zero” threshold.
Once the ball’s speed dropped below a small value, I forced it to stop and advanced the turn.
One line of logic fixed the entire multiplayer flow.
If your game logic depends on something ending, you can’t rely on “almost zero.”
You need to define what zero actually means.
I wrote a deeper postmortem about building this game in a week - including procedural generation, multiplayer decisions, and what I’d do differently next time - here:
👉 [https://medium.com/@chaarasvarun/7-games-in-7-weeks-building-backyard-golf-on-rune-week-2-0fd3737f935f]
articles.title: I Lost a Week to a Physics Bug in a Multiplayer Golf Game

articles.author: Saiki Sarkar
articles.description:
Introducing Nano Banana Pro’s AI-Powered Innovation

In a groundbreaking advancement for presentation technology, BananaTech has announced full editability for its Nano Banana Pro slides within the Manus collaborative platform. This integration marks the first instance of AI-driven presentation tools achieving real-time collaborative editing parity with traditional slide software.

## The Manus Integration: A Game-Changer for Real-Time Editing

Until now, AI-generated presentations existed in walled gardens—users could export static files but couldn't collaboratively refine AI-created content within team environments. The Nano Banana Pro/Manus integration changes this paradigm through three revolutionary features: bidirectional sync architecture that maintains AI metadata, version-controlled suggestion layers that distinguish human edits from AI foundations, and dynamic resource optimization that preserves computational integrity during multi-user sessions.

## Implications for the Future of Presentation Design

This development fundamentally alters how enterprises approach content creation workflows. Marketing teams can now iterate on AI-generated campaign pitches simultaneously across continents. Educators gain the ability to co-develop lecture materials while preserving accessibility enhancements auto-generated by Nano Banana Pro's algorithms. Perhaps most significantly, the integration sets a new benchmark for interoperability between specialized AI tools and established productivity ecosystems—a crucial step toward mainstream adoption of generative technologies in professional environments where collaboration is non-negotiable.
articles.title: Nano Banana Pro Slides Now Editable on Manus, Marking a First for AIPresentation Tools
